record.original_question: Can one characterize classes of gems for which the trisections arising from those gems actually realize the trisection genus of the represented 4-manifolds? In other words, beyond merely producing or bounding trisections from gems, which combinatorial or topological conditions on a gem guarantee that the trisection obtained from it has minimum possible genus for the underlying 4-manifold?

evidence.quote: With respect to Section 3.2, a fundamental problem involves the possible characterization of classes of gems so that the arising trisections (either directly, as gem-induced trisections, or indirectly, via the approach described in Section 3.2.2) realize the trisection genus of the represented 4-manifolds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A gem (graph-encoded manifold) of a compact PL 4-manifold M is a regular 5-edge-colored graph (G, γ) with γ : E(G) → {0,1,2,3,4}, encoding M as follows: take one 4-simplex for each vertex of G, label its 5 vertices by the colors 0,...,4, and identify pairs of facets across each c-colored edge of G by matching their unlabeled-by-c vertex tuples; the resulting pseudomanifold has M as a regular neighborhood of its 1-skeleton (in the closed orientable case it is M itself).

A trisection of a closed orientable 4-manifold M is a decomposition M = X_1 ∪ X_2 ∪ X_3 where each X_i ≅ ♮^{k_i}(S^1 × B^3), pairwise intersections X_i ∩ X_j are 3-dimensional handlebodies, and the triple intersection X_1 ∩ X_2 ∩ X_3 is a closed orientable surface Σ_g (the central surface). The genus g is called the genus of the trisection. The trisection genus g(M) of M is the minimum g over all trisections of M.

From any gem of a closed orientable 4-manifold M one can construct (directly, or via an intermediate procedure based on colored triangulations of associated singular manifolds) a trisection T(G,γ) of M, called a gem-induced trisection, whose genus g(T(G,γ)) bounds g(M) from above.

Problem. Find combinatorial and/or topological conditions on a 5-colored gem (G, γ) of a closed orientable PL 4-manifold M that are necessary and sufficient (or at least sufficient) to guarantee that the genus of the associated gem-induced trisection equals the trisection genus g(M). Equivalently, characterize the classes of gems whose gem-induced trisections are genus-minimizing for the represented 4-manifold.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on gem-induced trisections (Casali–Cristofori, 2019/2024) shows that for certain classes of simply-connected 4-manifolds the G-trisection genus coincides with the trisection genus (equal to b_2), but a general characterization of which gems produce genus-minimizing trisections is explicitly listed as a fundamental open problem in the relationships-and-open-problems survey on Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems. No source claims a full characterization.

status_evidence.title: Gem-induced trisections of compact PL 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Gem-induced trisections fit the definition of trisection for a suitable class of closed orientable 4-manifolds; G-trisection genus equals trisection genus for some standard classes.
status_evidence.claim: A characterization in general is not provided; equality of G-trisection genus and trisection genus is only established for restricted classes.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: A fundamental problem involves the possible characterization of classes of gems so that the arising trisections realize the trisection genus of the represented 4-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open.
